q: 1. The contractor is responsible for
options: procuring material which is not supplied by the owner
organizing and planning the work as per drawing
executing the work as per specifications laid down in the contract
explain: A contractor's overall responsibility covers material procurement (where not owner-supplied), planning, and execution per specifications - all of the above.

q: 2. In the analysis of rate, the profit for the contractor is generally taken as
explain: In standard rate analysis practice, contractor's profit margin is conventionally taken as 15% of the cost.

q: 3. The best method of procurement for complex and work of specific nature is
explain: Complex, specialised works need wide competition and expertise, so International Competitive Bidding (ICB) is used.

q: 4. Site order book is used for recoding
options: indents for materials to be ordered
explain: The site order book records the engineer's instructions to the contractor.

q: 5. Contractor is liable to maintain the defects upto
explain: The contractor must rectify defects during the defect liability period.

q: 6. The formula for determination of price adjustment in a work contract may not contain
explain: Price adjustment formulas typically use contract price, adjustment amount, and material/labour price indices, but do not directly include equipment cost as a variable.

q: 7. Bidding document is prepared
explain: Bidding documents must be finalized and prepared before the tender notice is published so bidders can obtain and use them.

q: 8. Security deposit deducted from contractor's bill is
options: refunded when the contractor has completed the work
refunded even before the completion of the work provided good progress has been established
retained till the expected life of the structure of say 100 years and spent for maintenance
refunded when the defect liability period is over
explain: Security deposit is retained as protection against defects and is refunded only after the defect liability period expires satisfactorily.

q: 9. Pre-Qualification document should be approved by
explain: D would have been the beast answer but AS PER BOOK A .Depending on the level and type of public entity, pre-qualification documents can be approved by the Director General, chief of public entity, or a class-I gazetted office chief - any of the above.

q: 10. A document containing detailed description of all the items of work (but their quantities are not mentioned) together with their current rates is called
explain: A schedule of rates lists item descriptions and their current unit rates without specifying quantities, unlike a tender document or estimate.

q: 11. The Contractor is responsible for
options: procuring material which is not supplied by the owner
organising and planning the work as per drawing
executing the work as per specifications laid down on the contact
explain: All three are contractor duties.

q: 12. The tender is
options: Written offer submitted by contractor to execute works
explain: A tender is the written offer submitted by a contractor proposing to execute the specified works at quoted rates/terms.

q: 13. The pre qualification criteria is approved by
explain: Per the answer key, the department head.

q: 14. Which types of tender generally prefer
explain: Schedule of Rates (SOR) is preferred in civil engineering works as it allows for payments based on actual quantities measured at agreed rates.

q: 15. Local tender is not favorable due to following reasons:
options: most of the material used locally
engineer or site in charge pressurized
explain: Local tenders can sometimes lead to localized pressure or influence on the decision-making staff compared to international competitive bidding.

q: 16. Quality and cost based selection (QCBS) method is used
options: Progress of work up to a stage
explain: QCBS is a standard method used to select consultants by evaluating both technical quality and cost of their proposals.

q: 17. The amount of earnest money generally deposited at the time of submission of tender is
explain: In Nepal's Public Procurement Act, bid security (earnest money) is usually 2% to 3% of the estimated amount.

q: 18. Amicable settlement means
explain: Amicable settlement is a non-adversarial process where the parties resolve the dispute themselves through negotiation.

q: 19. What are the essential components of a valid contract?
explain: An enforceable contract mandates mutual offer/acceptance, free consent, legal capacity, and consideration[cite: 1].

q: 20. The types of contract followed in Middle-Marsyangdi hydro electricity project is
explain: Major public civil engineering works like hydro projects typically utilize item rate contracts[cite: 1].

q: 21. Force majeure in a contract is
options: occurrence of an event beyond the control of both the parties of the contract
occurrence of an event beyond the control of the contractor
occurrence of an event beyond the control of the employer
explain: Force majeure refers to unforeseeable events beyond the control of both contracting parties (e.g., natural disasters), excusing performance delays.

q: 22. The opening of bidding in the process of procurement is
explain: Tendering opens the bidding process.

q: 23. Consulting works worth more than 10 crores NRs should be procured on the basis of
explain: Per the answer key, international-level EOI and RFP.

q: 24. For the construction of a project, a contractor is a
explain: A contractor can be a legally registered individual, a partnership firm, or a corporate agency.

q: 25. The maximum amount for approval of tender by Gazetted 3rd class officer is (Source:PPR 2064(67))
explain: Standard delegation of authority limits a 3rd class officer to tenders below 10 Crore (100 million).

q: 26. The minimum no. of parties for doing any contract/agreement should be
explain: A contract requires a minimum of two parties: the promisor and the promisee.

q: 27. At present, in Nepal the types of contract normally followed in housing project to save the government taxes is
explain: In small-scale housing, owners often provide materials themselves and contract only for labor to reduce tax liability.

q: 28. *The amount of money deposited by successful bidder as a security for satisfactory performance is called
explain: Performance security is provided by the winning bidder to protect the owner against non-performance.

q: 29. Contractor's prequalification is required for project cost above (Source:PPR2064(3))
explain: Prequalification is mandatory for large-scale projects, typically those exceeding 20 million in value.

q: 30. The various types of contract are
explain: These are all standard methods of contracting used in the construction industry.

q: 31. The amount of money paid to the contractor by the client after the agreement and before the execution of work, is known as
explain: Mobilization advance is an advance payment made to the contractor after signing the agreement to help setup initial site operations and resources.

q: 32. The earnest money deposited by unsuccessful bidder is returned after
explain: Per the answer key, after the contract is awarded to the successful bidder.

q: 33. Power stations are generally treated as
explain: Power plants involve complex machinery and specific structural requirements that classify them as industrial projects.

q: 34. Force Majeure in a contract is:
options: Occurrence of an act beyond the control of both the parties in contract agreement
Preventing both parties to perform the respective obligation agreed
explain: Force majeure encompasses both the occurrence of an uncontrollable event and its effect of preventing both parties from performing their obligations - both A and B.

q: 35. An offer in writing to execute some specified civil works at certain rates within a fixed time under certain conditions of contract is called :
explain: A bid (or tender) is the formal written offer submitted by a contractor in response to an invitation to work.

q: 36. An EPC contract means:
explain: EPC stands for Engineering, Procurement, and Construction—a form of turnkey agreement where one contractor handles total delivery.

q: 37. "Fraudulent Practice" means
options: The offering, giving, receiving of anything of value of influence the action of a public official in the procurement process
Misrepresentation of facts to influence a procurement process
explain: Fraudulent practice covers both improper inducement of officials and misrepresentation of facts - both a and b.

q: 38. Contractor's prequalification is required for:
explain: Prequalification is required specifically for major and specialized works needing verified contractor capability.

q: 39. Percentage of retention money is equal to ……… % of each payment made to the contractor.
explain: Per the answer key, 5%.

q: 40. As per public the public procurement regulation 2064, who approves the prequalification criteria?
explain: Per the answer key, the concerned department chief.
